EXECUTIVE ORDER 10283
Creating  a B oard of I nquiry  T o R eport 
on  C ertain  L abor D isputes  A ffecting  
the  C opper  and N o n-F errous  M etals  
I ndustry
WHEREAS there exist certain labor 
disputes between Kennecott Copper Cor­
poration, Phelps Dodge Corporation, 
American Smelting and Refining Com­
pany, Anaconda Copper Mining Com­
pany, including International Smelting 
and Refining Company, and other em­
ployers who are similarly engaged in 
mining,- milling, smelting, or refining 
copper or other non-ferrous metals and 
certain of their employees represented 
by certain labor organizations, including 
the International Union of Mine, Mill 
and Smelter Workers, several Railroad 
Brotherhoods, and-unions affiliated with 
the American Federation of Labor; and 
WHEREAS in my opinion such dis­
putes have resulted, or threaten to result, 
in strikes or lockouts affecting a substan­
tial part of the copper and non-ferrous 
metals industry, an industry engaged in 
trade and commerce among the several 
states and with foreign nations, and in 
the production of goods for commerce, 
which strikes or lockouts, if permitted to 
occur or continue, will imperil the na­
tional health and safety;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 206 of 
the Labor-Management Relations Act, 
1947 (Public Law 101, 80th Congress), I  
hereby create a Board of Inquiry, con­
sisting of such members as I  shall 
appoint, to inquire into the issues in­
volved in such disputes.
The Board shall have powers and 
duties as set forth in Title II of the said 
Act. The Board shall report to the Pres­
ident in accordance with the provisions 
of section 206 of the said Act on or before 
September fourth, 1951.
Upon the submission of its report, the 
Board shall continue in existence to per­
form such other functions as may be 
required under the said Act, until the 
Board is terminated by the President.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10283 (16 FR 8873; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10283 and signed August 30, 1951. The order creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 to inquire into the issues in a labor dispute affecting the copper and non-ferrous metals industry, with a report due on a stated date and a provision that, once the report is submitted, the Board continues in existence to perform other functions required under the Act until the President terminates it. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the Board, its report date, and its continuation until terminated by the President are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10283 with a subject line matching this order (creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.

EO 12553 is itself a presidential revocation of the order by number and is the first held instrument ending it. (3) No later order amends or supersedes it in the held corpus. savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.
